subject: environmental-science
title: Particles, Plumes and PM2.5
welcome_lead: From smog to seabeds — track pollutants from source to fate.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on air pollutants, dispersion and human health impacts.
final_note: PM2.5 is small enough to cross alveolar membranes — a global killer measured in micrograms.

concepts.def: Particulate matter <2.5 μm diameter, capable of alveolar penetration.
Oxides of nitrogen (NO, NO₂) from combustion; precursors to ozone and acid rain.
Sulphur oxides from fossil fuel burning; cause acidification of rain (pH <5.6).
Secondary pollutant formed by NOx + VOCs + sunlight; damages lungs and crops.
Vehicle exhaust device that reduces NOx, CO and unburnt HC using Pt-Pd-Rh.

walkthroughs.body_html: Primary pollutants (PM, NOx, SOx, CO) are emitted directly. Secondary pollutants (O₃, PAN, sulphate aerosol) form in the atmosphere via photochemistry.
PM2.5 exposure causes ~7 million premature deaths yr⁻¹ (WHO). It triggers oxidative stress, inflammation and cardiovascular events.
Three-way catalysts cut NOx, CO and HC. Flue-gas desulphurisation removes SO₂ from power station emissions using limestone slurry.

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Predators have weaker immune systems.
Bacteria produce them.
Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: Bacteria produce them.
They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
